label: Topological Spaces
notes: This chapter spans printed pages nineteen through forty-eight and replaces distance with open sets as the primitive data. We build a computational test bench for topology, basis, continuity, Hausdorff, second countable, and locally Euclidean, then assemble the three-lock gate that defines a topological manifold of one fixed dimension.

label: What Is a Topology
notes: A topology is a chosen collection of open subsets closed under three operations. The empty set and the whole space are open, arbitrary unions stay open, and finite intersections stay open. On a finite set every union is enumerable, so these axioms become an exact closure checklist we can run by hand.

label: Three Standard Topologies
notes: Every set carries at least two topologies. The discrete topology makes every subset open and separates all points. The trivial topology offers only the empty set and the whole space. The metric topology, generated by open balls, is the bridge from Euclidean geometry into the abstract open-set language used throughout the book.

label: Bases and Subbases
notes: A basis compresses a topology into basic open sets whose unions recover every open set. Validity needs two conditions: the basic sets cover the space, and each overlap is locally refined by a smaller basic set through the point. A subbasis is even looser, generating a basis through finite intersections first.

label: Closed Sets
notes: Closed sets are exactly the complements of open sets, so the axioms dualize. The whole space and empty set are closed, arbitrary intersections of closed sets are closed, and finite unions are closed. In a non-Hausdorff space a single point need not be closed, which already signals trouble for limits.

label: Interior, Closure, Boundary
notes: For a subset, the interior is the largest open set inside it, the closure is the smallest closed set containing it, and the boundary is the closure minus the interior. These three nested regions are computed by asking which neighborhoods fit inside and which neighborhoods are forced to meet the subset.

label: Neighborhoods
notes: A neighborhood of a point is any open set containing it. In a finite topology the intersection of all neighborhoods of a point gives a minimal open neighborhood. The specialization preorder records when every open set around one point also drags a second point along, the finite shadow of failed separation.

label: Continuity via Open Sets
notes: A map is continuous exactly when the preimage of every open set is open. This definition needs no metric. When the target has a basis it suffices to test preimages of basis elements, which is the workflow used throughout manifold theory where we check coordinate balls rather than every open subset.

label: Homeomorphisms
notes: A homeomorphism is a continuous bijection with a continuous inverse, the isomorphism of topology. Homeomorphic spaces share every property phrased in open sets, so they are indistinguishable as topological spaces. This is the equivalence under which a coffee mug and a doughnut are genuinely the same one-holed surface.

label: The Hausdorff Condition
notes: Hausdorffness promises that distinct points are separable by disjoint neighborhoods. Metric spaces satisfy it automatically using balls of radius below half the distance. Without it, sequences can converge to several limits and finite sets need not be closed. The Sierpinski space is the smallest finite witness of this failure.

label: Second Countability
notes: A space is second countable when one countable basis generates the whole topology. This single size condition implies first countability, separability, and the Lindelof property, so countable subcovers always exist. Euclidean space qualifies through balls with rational centers and rational radii, a countable family that still generates everything.

label: The Manifold Definition
notes: A topological manifold of dimension n is locally Euclidean of that fixed dimension, Hausdorff, and second countable. The three locks are independent. The doubled-origin line is locally line-like yet not Hausdorff, while finite non-discrete spaces fail the local chart test, so no single condition can be dropped.

label: Recap and Outlook
notes: Open sets are the primitive data from which closure, interior, continuity, and separation are derived. A basis compresses a topology; Hausdorff and second countable are structural safeguards. The manifold gate combines locally Euclidean of one dimension with both safeguards, and half-space charts extend the idea to manifolds with boundary.
